title: Drop the quadratic parameter scan in composite Model.eval
problem: Model.make_funcargs scans every parameter and calls _strip_prefix for every component. A composite of P prefixed peaks therefore does O(P^2) Python work on each Model.eval, which Model.fit calls on every residual. On an 80-peak Gaussian sum, cProfile shows make_funcargs and _strip_prefix taking about 94% of eval time. This is a different path from the merged NaN-mask change in coerce_float64 (PR 1063). Closed PR 997 only suggested storing _func_allargs as a set and was not merged. Open PRs 1015 and 1018 do not change make_funcargs.
approach: For a prefixed model whose function has no **kwargs, read only that component's arguments: for each function argument, the parameter named prefix+argument, and the bare argument when that name does not start with the prefix. Evaluate .value in params insertion order, then re-read self._param_names so a prefixed parameter still overwrites an unprefixed one. Build the insertion-order map once per top-level Model.eval or CompositeModel.eval and share it with nested components. Keep the existing full scan for unprefixed models, **kwargs functions, strip=False, and direct make_funcargs calls. Keep the keyword overwrite and the saved-value restore.
result_constraint: Returned arrays and fit outputs stay the same, including expression order. A private implementation matched Model.eval exactly on a reverse within-component expression, on 60 random composite models, and on a constrained 6-peak fit. A 40-peak fit capped at 25 evaluations matched residual, best_values, chisqr, and nfev exactly (chisqr 9400.078433862305). The same patch still passed the native suite: 790 passed, 30 skipped.
observed_effect: On this machine the private patch made this harness's 80-peak eval about 3.9x faster and a 160-peak eval about 5.9x faster. The same patch made a 40-peak Model.fit with max_nfev=25 about 1.52x faster (median about 0.083s to 0.053s) with identical residuals. Those patched times are not the baseline.
benchmark_protocol: OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR threads set to 1, taskset -c 0, one warmup eval, then 5 rounds. Each round is the median of 7 evals. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median*100 of those 5 medians. Workload: 80 GaussianModel peaks, 2000 x points, g{i}_sigma expr tied to g0_sigma. Checksum of the warmup eval is 39980.00000000001.
